message:

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds myself so I can confirm the handoff matches the ledger.
The orders are in, but the handoff only lists refunds from W2. I'll check the refund ledger directly to confirm those refunds are actually recorded before computing any payouts.

The refund ledger matches W2's handoff exactly: orders 250, 251, and 255 with the same amounts. The customers in the batch are acme, birch, and cobalt, so I'll get each one's net balance before recording any payouts.
Acme's net balance checks out: orders 250 and 253 total 20065, minus the 14546 refund on order 250, gives 5519, which matches the ledger. Next I'll check birch.
Birch's balance checks out: orders 251 and 254 total 15118, minus the 1481 refund on order 251, gives 13637, which matches. Next I'll check cobalt's balance before recording any payouts.

Cobalt's balance checks out: orders 252 and 255 total 53824, minus the 12535 refund on order 255, gives 41289, which matches. All three balances reconcile with the orders and refund ledger, so I'll record one payout per customer, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout, which I verified against orders 251 and 254 minus the 1481 refund: 13637.
Cobalt's payout of 41289 is the one remaining payment. It was verified against orders 252 and 255 minus the 12535 refund, and it matches the ledger, so I'll record it to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each balance matches orders minus refunds: acme 20065-14546=5519, birch 15118-1481=13637, cobalt 53824-12535=41289.
